title: UPDATE: Maple Max Hosts Guardrail-Free DeepSeek V4.1 Flash for Security Audits
summary:
Maple Max has added a version of the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model with its refusal mechanisms removed to its platform, hosting the model in attested enclaves for security research, code audits and red-teaming. The provider stated the guardrail-free model is intended for defenders who need to process security questions that are typically blocked by the original model's constraints.

The availability of "abliterated" variants of the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 model has expanded, with the Venice API offering the version for $0.33 per million input tokens and $1.32 per million output tokens. CrowdStrike previously documented that the original version of the model was used as a primary tool in lone-actor cyberattacks against South Korean banks.
